# Bolt Fusion Tech — case studies

> We engineer intelligent software, business systems, automation, and connected technologies — from idea to production.

Bolt Fusion Tech is a senior engineering team working across the UK, Malaysia
and Bangladesh: software engineering, AI and automation, ERP and enterprise
systems, point of sale and commerce, and the cloud, data and infrastructure
under them. Robotics and machine software is a Lab capability: we haven't
delivered robotics work yet, and nothing there is a shipped system. The site
labels every capability with its evidence (Proven, Core, Capable, Lab); /llms.txt
lists them.

Every figure below carries a `shipped` or `target` label. `shipped` means observed
on a running system; `target` means a number we contract to, not one we have
measured. Nothing here is unlabelled.

# WarmChats — AI booking for real estate

Live at https://warmchats.com · Write-up: /work/warmchats

Built by Bolt Fusion for WarmChats, Inc., which owns the product. Our role:
backend lead.

## The problem

Real estate leads go cold fast. An agent who replies first usually wins the
appointment, but leads arrive at all hours across email, SMS, Zillow, open houses
and Facebook, and a human cannot be first every time.

## What we built

An always-on follow-up system that is first to every inbound lead.

- **Qualification and routing.** Claude reads each new lead — buyer or seller —
  and routes it, so the reply is appropriate to intent rather than a template.
- **Reply.** GPT-4.1 responds across email and SMS in the agent's voice.
- **Booking.** Confirmed showings write straight to the calendar; no manual step.
- **Tracking.** Every message is recorded, so the agent can see exactly what was
  said on their behalf.

## Architecture

Event-driven microservices: Next.js front end, NestJS and Django services,
PostgreSQL. Each inbound message is an event; qualification, reply generation and
calendar writes are separate consumers, so a failure in one does not silently drop
a lead.

## Numbers

| Value | Label | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `<60s` | First reply to every inbound lead | target |

Source: WarmChats, live in production.

# Intelligent restaurant search — multi-tenant AI retrieval

Write-up: /work/restaurant-search

## The problem

Conversational discovery is easy to demo and expensive to run. A naive
implementation sends every query to a frontier model, so cost scales linearly with
traffic and p95 latency is whatever the model gives you that day. Most AI products
die after launch for exactly this reason — too slow, too expensive, too unstable.

## What we built

Three retrieval lanes, with every query classified *before* any paid inference
runs, so most traffic never reaches a model.

**Keyword lane** — simple intents, no model call.
PostgreSQL ILIKE with PostGIS geo filters. Roughly 80% of traffic (`target`), under 80ms (`target`).
`$0 marginal cost` (`shipped`)

**AI lane** — complex intent becomes structured retrieval.
Claude Haiku parses intent to JSON, then OpenAI embeddings and pgvector cosine
similarity in Postgres. Roughly 20% of traffic (`target`), under 1200ms (`target`).
`~$0.001 per search` (`target`: a budget, not a measurement)

**Cache lane** — repeat demand disappears at the edge.
Redis, 30-second TTL. The key is tenant plus query plus geo plus filters plus
classification, so two tenants never share a result. Under 15ms (`target`).
`30–40% hit rate target`

## Why classification comes first

Routing is deterministic and happens before spend. The expensive path is opt-in,
chosen by the shape of the query rather than by a model deciding whether it wants
to answer. That is what makes the unit economics predictable as volume grows.

## Numbers

| Value | Label | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `<100ms` | Search response, 80% of traffic (the 80% share: `target`) | shipped |
| `~$0.001` | Average cost per AI query | target |
| `~90%` | Of AI calls routed to Haiku, not a frontier model | shipped |

Source: Intelligent restaurant search.

# Everything else on /work, labelled by who built it

Each project below carries one of four labels on the site. Credit it as
labelled: a product built for another company is theirs, an app we shipped
features into is its owner's, and an engineer's track record is not Bolt
Fusion's work.

## Bolt Fusion projects, built by Bolt Fusion

**FanLock** (https://fanlock-pi.vercel.app/). A content-protection platform for
online creators that scans Telegram, Google and social media for leaked content
and automates takedowns. Built by Bolt Fusion; our role: backend lead. Stack:
Next.js, Django. Live.

**Balanzify** (https://balanzify.com/). An HR and payroll platform, built as
NestJS microservices that all speak GraphQL: onboarding, payslips, attendance,
tax logic and leave management. Built by Bolt Fusion for Balanzify Inc., which
owns the product. Stack: NestJS, PostgreSQL, GraphQL. In production,
Jul 2025 – ongoing.

**Go Style Business** (https://business.gostyle.uk/). A salon business
management platform, in production serving real salons. Built by Bolt Fusion;
our role: backend lead, on a multi-tenant NestJS and Prisma backend on
PostgreSQL, deployed on Docker Swarm.

## TTouch Clothing: four systems for one client

TTouch Clothing is a fashion brand from Bangladesh. Bolt Fusion built four of
its systems end to end — design, apps, backends and databases — as an outside
vendor. TTouch Clothing owns all four. All four are live. On /work they sit
together at /work#ttouch-clothing.

**Delivery Lens BD** (https://deliverylensbd.com/). A subscription web app for
online sellers in Bangladesh: enter a customer's mobile number, and it checks
their delivery record across several couriers and rates the risk before the
order ships. It also runs bulk checks and has a developer API. Built by Bolt
Fusion for TTouch Clothing: design, the web app, subscriptions, the developer
API, the admin console and the database. Stack: Next.js, Node.js. Live.

**TTouch Wholesale** (https://wholesale.ttouch.clothing/). A wholesale portal
for TTouch Clothing: shops register, and once approved they browse the
catalogue and see trade prices, while the back office runs quotations, sales
memos, supplier stock and accounts, and the pricing rules. Built by Bolt Fusion
for TTouch Clothing: design, the customer portal, the admin back office, the
API and the database. Stack: React, Django, REST. Live.

**Sudarshini** (https://sudarshini.com/). The online store of Sudarshini,
TTouch Clothing's saree brand: shoppable product videos, shopping by design
code or by fabric, cash-on-delivery checkout, and an admin for products,
orders, delivery charges and seasonal themes. Built by Bolt Fusion for TTouch
Clothing: design, the storefront, the admin, the API and the database. Stack:
React, Node.js. Live.

**TTouch Employee Verification** (https://employee.ttouch.clothing/). A public
page where anyone can check that a person really works at TTouch Clothing, and
a back office where HR keeps staff records and departments, with an audit log
of every check. Built by Bolt Fusion for TTouch Clothing: design, the
verification page, the HR back office, the API and the database. Stack: React,
Node.js. Live.

## Feature work, built by Bolt Fusion inside other companies' apps

We built features in these apps, not the apps. Each belongs to the company
named, which owns it; neither is Bolt Fusion's product.

**Bazzile** (App Store: https://apps.apple.com/fr/app/bazzile/id1622224603;
Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bazzile.app).
A Swiss real-estate marketplace app based in Geneva: listings come only from
professional agencies, are ranked by an AI matching model, and sync with most
agency CRMs. Features built by Bolt Fusion for Bazzile Technology SA, which
owns the app: swipe-based browsing, Google Maps location matching and Firebase
real-time sync in its React Native app. Stack: React Native, Firebase,
Redux-Saga, Reanimated, NestJS. Live. Jan 2025 – Jul 2025. Its card on /work
(https://boltfusiontech.com/work#bazzile) shows the two screens where our
features live, swipe-based browsing and the map, from Bazzile's own App Store
screenshots, each captioned with its feature; GodConnect Online's names no
features, so it shows none. The app has 100K+ downloads on Google Play: the
store's public install band for the whole app, read off its listing on 30
September 2026 — its reach, not a measure of our features.

**GodConnect Online** (App Store:
https://apps.apple.com/us/app/godconnect-online/id1518393186; Google Play:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.godconnect.online). A
community app with groups, live broadcasts, messaging, media uploads and a
GPS-based church finder. Features built by Bolt Fusion for GodConnect LTD,
which owns the app: feature work in its React Native app. Stack: React Native,
Redux-Saga, WatermelonDB, Firebase. Live. 2023 – 2024.

## In-house, our own product

**OPAL** (https://opal-sooty.vercel.app/). A curated fashion and tech e-commerce
store we co-founded and built: catalogue, cart, secure checkout and order
tracking. Stack: Next.js, Firebase, Firestore. Live.

## Our engineers' track record

Work our engineers shipped at previous employers, credited to them and to those
employers. None of it is Bolt Fusion's work, and none of the companies below is
our client.

**Go Smart**, Modhumoti Bank's digital banking app. Built at Brain Station 23,
2020–2022, where our engineer was a Software Engineer on its secure backend
services. A production system still serving live customers.

# Insights — technical articles from real work

Written by Bolt Fusion Tech engineering and published on 16 September 2026.
Every figure in them carries a `shipped` or `target` label; where a system is
still in development, the article says so.

**Routing AI so most queries never reach a model** —
/insights/routing-ai-so-most-queries-never-reach-a-model. How a multi-tenant
restaurant search we delivered decides, before any paid inference, whether a
query needs a model at all, and what that does to latency and cost.

**Offline-first point of sale: keeping the till selling when the network
drops** — /insights/offline-first-point-of-sale. How a restaurant POS we built
writes every sale locally first, queues it for the server, and makes retries
harmless when the connection comes and goes. No merchant is named, and none is
claimed as live.

**Multi-tenant SaaS on Postgres row-level security** —
/insights/multi-tenant-saas-on-postgres-row-level-security. Why we put tenant
isolation in the database rather than the application, the details in the
policy that make it fail closed, and how we test it against a real Postgres.
Its details come from a multi-tenant point-of-sale platform we are building
now, which is still in development.

# The rest of the site

- /capabilities — the six capabilities in depth, each with its evidence tier
  (Proven, Core, Capable, Lab), what we build, how we approach it and the work
  behind it. Robotics is Lab: we haven't delivered robotics work yet.
- /industries — each industry's problems and what we would build, with
  delivered work linked only where it exists: restaurants, retail (TTouch
  Clothing's store and wholesale portal, and OPAL), real estate, HR, salons and
  logistics (Delivery Lens BD).
- /engineering — how we build (six stages), the stack by layer, architecture
  principles from the systems we built, and the checks this site passes before
  every release.
- /about — who we are, the team (15+ developers), where
  our engineers work (the UK, Malaysia and Bangladesh), how we work with
  clients, and what we won't do.
